intro: Installing a wet room in Crichton isn't quite the same as fitting one in a modern city-centre flat. The properties here — a mix of solid stone cottages, older period homes, and newer estate builds — each come with their own quirks that need proper consideration before a single tile goes down. Done well, a wet room adds real value and genuine day-to-day comfort, particularly for households where accessibility matters. Done poorly, it becomes an expensive waterproofing problem. If you're weighing up a wet room installation in Crichton, understanding what's involved from the outset will save you time, money, and a lot of frustration down the line.
localContext: Crichton's housing stock is part of what makes installation planning here genuinely interesting. The older stone-built properties and period cottages in the area typically have solid floors rather than timber suspended ones, which can actually work in your favour — solid bases are easier to waterproof reliably and better suited to the linear drains and tanking systems used in modern wet rooms. That said, stone walls can present challenges with moisture management, and getting the right membrane system matters more than it might in a newer build. The modern estates in Crichton are a different story: timber joists and chipboard subfloors need careful structural assessment and often require additional work to create a suitable base for a wet room installation. Crichton also sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth factoring in when choosing your fixtures — limescale build-up on frameless screens and chrome fittings is a real consideration, and investing in a quality shower head with easy-clean nozzles will pay off over time.
serviceDetail: A proper wet room installation in Crichton typically unfolds across several stages, and a good installer will walk you through each one before any work begins. The process starts with a thorough survey of your existing bathroom space — checking floor structure, drainage position, ceiling height, and the condition of existing pipework. This survey shapes everything else, including whether any structural reinforcement is needed and where the waste outlet will sit. Next comes the waterproofing stage, which is arguably the most important part of the whole job. A tanking system — usually a combination of liquid membrane and reinforced tape at joints — is applied across the floor and up the walls to a minimum height. Getting this stage right is non-negotiable; any shortcut here will eventually result in water finding its way into your subfloor or walls. Once the tanking is cured and checked, the floor is screeded to the correct fall angle (typically around 1:80 gradient towards the drain), which ensures water flows away efficiently without pooling. Tiling, fitting the linear drain, installing the shower valve, screen, and any additional fixtures follows. In Crichton's older properties especially, it's common to discover old pipework that needs upgrading at this point — which is better dealt with during the installation than left to become a problem later. The final stage is grouting, sealing, and a thorough test of all drainage and water connections before handover.
pricing: Wet room installations in Crichton typically fall in the range of £6,000 to £12,000, depending on the size of the space, the complexity of the existing structure, and the quality of materials chosen. A straightforward installation in a modern estate property with an accessible floor void will generally sit at the lower end. An older stone cottage requiring floor reinforcement, re-routing of pipework, or bespoke tiling work will move towards the higher end. Premium fixtures — quality linear drains, designer tiles, thermostatic shower systems — add cost but also add lasting value. Always get a written, itemised quote that separates labour from materials so you can make fair comparisons.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson familiar with Crichton and the surrounding Midlothian area makes a practical difference on a job like this. Local installers will have worked in similar stone-built properties and period cottages before — they won't be surprised by what they find when they open up a floor or chase into a wall. They'll also have working relationships with local suppliers, which can help with lead times on materials and means any snagging issues get resolved quickly rather than waiting weeks for someone to travel out. For a premium planned project like a wet room, that local knowledge and accountability genuinely matters.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Crichton?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's done regularly in properties like these across Midlothian. Solid stone floors are actually well-suited to wet room installations. The main considerations are ensuring the walls are properly tanked to manage moisture, and that any old pipework is assessed at the same time. A good installer will survey the property thoroughly before quoting.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Crichton?
faqs.a: Most wet room installations take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. The curing time for the tanking membrane accounts for some of that — it can't be rushed without risking the integrity of the waterproofing. More complex jobs in older properties, where pipework or structural work is involved, may take a few days longer.

faqs.q: Does hard water in Crichton affect which fittings I should choose?
faqs.a: It's worth considering, yes. Crichton sits in a moderately hard water area, so limescale will build up on fixtures over time. Opt for shower heads with silicone nozzles that wipe clean easily, and consider a thermostatic valve with a good warranty. Regular use of a squeegee on screens and a mild descaler on fittings will keep everything looking good longer.

faqs.q: Will a wet room add value to my Crichton property?
faqs.a: A well-installed wet room generally adds value, particularly in family homes and properties where accessibility is a selling point. In Crichton's mix of period and modern homes, a high-quality wet room that complements the character of the property tends to be viewed positively by buyers. Poor installation or cheap finishes can have the opposite effect, which is why quality of workmanship matters here.
